newsitem.title: YEMEN: Ruling party heads for landslide win in Yemen poll.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party heads for landslide win in Yemen poll.

text.p: Yemen's ruling General Peoples Congress (GPC) was headed for a sweeping victory on Thursday by winning 184 seats as vote-counting continued in elections to the country's 301-member parliament.

A statement by Yemen's Supreme Election Committee also said the Islah Party, the GPC's Islamist junior coalition partner, won 47 seat while 49 went to independents and five seats to two opposition parties.

Final results in the country's first parliamentary poll since a 1994 civil war were expected on Thursday, but it was not immediately clear whether the winners of the remaining 16 seats would be announced as planned.
Islah has accused the Supreme Elections Committee of bias, threatening court action.
At least 21 people have been killed in violence linked to Sunday's poll.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123 seats, Islah 62 and the Yemen Socialist Party 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties. The country was formed in 1990 by a merger of conservative North Yemen and Marxist South Yemen.
